key_insight: Training a retrieval-augmented foundation model on large-scale matched molecular pair transformations (MMPTs) lets the model generate diverse, controllable analog edits that recapitulate medicinal chemistry intuition. The variable-to-variable formulation focuses on local edits rather than whole-molecule rewriting, improving edit fidelity and transferability.
problem_solved: Existing ML approaches either model whole molecules with poor controllability over local edits or learn MMP-style edits only from small, restricted datasets; this work scales MMPT learning and adds retrieval context to recover chemists' intuitive transformations.
method: Formulate analog generation as a variable-to-variable task that directly models local chemical edits (matched molecular pairs) instead of full-molecule generation.
Train a foundation model on large-scale MMPT data so it learns diverse edit patterns and conditional generation of analog variables.
Augment generation with a retrieval component that provides relevant historical MMP examples as context to guide controllable, chemistry-aware transformations.
impact: Enables scalable, controllable analog design that aligns with medicinal chemists' reasoning, improving iteration speed in lead optimization. Demonstrates that retrieval-augmented foundation models can capture domain-specific edit operators useful for broader AI-driven molecular design.

paper_title: Retrieval-Augmented Foundation Models for Matched Molecular Pair Transformations to Recapitulate Medicinal Chemistry Intuition
